title: Three Killed, Teen Arrested in Mass Shooting at Seattle Food Festival
excerpt: A 15-year-old suspect is in custody after gunfire at the annual Bite of Seattle festival near the Space Needle left three dead and four wounded, including a toddler.
body:
• Three people — two men aged 19 and 44 and a 56-year-old woman — were killed in a shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival on Sunday evening.
  • A 15-year-old suspect has been arrested and is being held in juvenile detention on firearms violations and first-degree assault charges, with a court appearance set for Monday.
  • Police believe two suspects exchanged gunfire and are still searching for a second individual who fled the scene.
  • Four others, including a two-year-old boy, were hospitalized in stable condition; questions about festival security have intensified after attendees reported no metal detectors or bag checks.

Three people were killed and four others wounded, including a two-year-old boy, when gunfire erupted at the annual Bite of Seattle food festival on Sunday evening, police said. A 15-year-old suspect has been arrested and is being held in juvenile detention, while a second suspect remains at large.

The shooting broke out at approximately 6:01 p.m. local time at the Seattle Center, the sprawling campus beneath the city's iconic Space Needle, where thousands of people had gathered for the final day of the three-day event.

What Happened

Seattle Police Department Assistant Chief Tyrone Davis said at a media briefing that officers believe two suspects exchanged gunfire at the festival. Dozens of officers were already patrolling the event grounds and some witnessed one of the suspects firing, according to Davis.

Two people were pronounced dead at the scene, and a third victim died after being transported to a local hospital. The victims were identified as two men, aged 19 and 44, and a 56-year-old woman. Four others sustained gunshot wounds to the arm, abdomen, and leg. All four, including the toddler, were in stable condition on Monday morning, according to Seattle Fire Department spokeswoman Grace Nuñez.

One suspect surrendered at the scene, while the other fled. The arrested suspect, a 15-year-old, is being investigated for firearms violations and first-degree assault and is scheduled to appear in court on Monday afternoon.

"What happened at the Seattle Center today was an act of horrific violence. Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives, and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire."

— Katie Wilson, Mayor of Seattle

Panic at the Festival

Witnesses described scenes of chaos as families scrambled for cover. Faith Adia Hunter said she and her friends had just bought food from a crêpe vendor when they heard gunfire and realized the shooter was nearby. "We were right next to him when it started so we took off running," Hunter told The Times. "We ran into the building with the crowd."

Estan Wakonabo, who was waiting in line for a photobooth with his girlfriend, said he was shoved from behind and turned to see a stampede. "People were hiding, pushing, people were falling to the ground, baby strollers were falling," he said.

Other witnesses described helping lift children over fences to safety as festivalgoers smashed through barriers to escape. Harrowing images from the scene showed an abandoned stroller among scattered tables and debris.

Security Under Scrutiny

The shooting has drawn immediate scrutiny over security at the event. A Washington-based content creator known as Leebo posted a TikTok video the day before the shooting expressing alarm at the apparent lack of precautions at the festival, according to the New York Post.

"There's not any security walking around," the TikTokker said in his video from Saturday. "You should not be able to just walk up into this festival — with all these people, with all these vendors — with no security." He said there were no pat-downs, bag checks, or metal detectors at the entrance.

The Bite of Seattle, which has taken place annually since 1982 and has been hosted at the Seattle Center since 1986, draws roughly 350,000 visitors over its three-day run. The free-to-attend event features hundreds of food vendors, craft beer and wine tastings, and live musical performances. It has twice been voted the best food festival in the United States.

A City Shaken

For the Indian-American community concentrated in the greater Seattle area — home to one of the largest South Asian populations in the country, anchored by the tech corridors of Bellevue and Redmond — the shooting struck close to home. The Bite of Seattle is a mainstay summer event widely attended by families across the region's diverse communities.

Davis said there was no continuing threat to the public but urged anyone with information about the second suspect to contact police. The investigation is ongoing, and authorities have not disclosed a motive for the shooting.

What's Next

The arrested 15-year-old suspect is expected to face a juvenile court hearing on Monday afternoon. Police continue to search for the second suspect who fled the scene. The festival grounds at Seattle Center remain closed as investigators process the crime scene. City officials have not yet announced whether enhanced security protocols will be imposed on future large-scale public events in Seattle.
nri_angle: The shooting at a major Seattle summer festival hits close to home for the large Indian-American community in the greater Seattle-Bellevue tech corridor.
author: Diaspora Desk
